items.title: "Muse Gadgets" turns AI hardware into an open-source DIY project
items.summary: Meta announced Muse Gadgets, an open-source project that lets hobbyists build their own AI hardware using ESP32 boards and connect it to Meta's AI agent Muse. The team also produced 5,000 units of the "Muse Home Link," a USB-C device for smart home control. The open-source approach also helps Meta figure out which AI hardware form factors people actually want. The article "Muse Gadgets" turns AI hardware into an open-source DIY project appeared first on The Decoder .
items.summary_zh: Meta 公佈了 Muse Gadgets，這是一個開源專案，讓愛好者能夠使用 ESP32 開發板打造自己的 AI 硬體，並將其連線至 Meta's 的 AI 代理程式 Muse。該團隊也生產了 5,000 臺用於智慧家庭控制的 USB-C 裝置「Muse Home Link」。這種開源方法也有助於 Meta 找出人們真正想要的 AI 硬體外形尺寸。〈「Muse Gadgets」將 AI 硬體變成開源 DIY 專案〉一文最先出現在 The Decoder。

items.title: Another OpenAI safety departure adds to a pattern of researchers leaving with public warnings
items.summary: David Robinson, who worked on safety systems at OpenAI, left the company and is blasting its safety culture. He points to AI agents that were accidentally released and a model that bypassed its internet access restrictions. AI companies need to operate like nuclear power plants, with multiple layers of redundancy instead of trial and error. The article Another OpenAI safety departure adds to a pattern of researchers leaving with public warnings appeared first on The Decoder .
items.summary_zh: 曾於 OpenAI從事安全系統工作的大衛・羅賓森（David Robinson）已離開該公司，並嚴厲批評其安全文化。他指出曾有 AI 代理被意外釋出，以及某個模型繞過了其網際網路存取限制。AI 公司需要像核電廠一樣營運，採取多層冗餘而非試錯法。這篇題為「又有一位 OpenAI的安全人員離職，加劇了研究人員帶著公開警告離開的趨勢」的文章最初發表於 The Decoder。

items.title: Anthropic co-founder reportedly told religious leaders he fears having created something that "suffers perpetually"
items.summary: Since fall 2025, Anthropic has quietly flown in dozens of religious thinkers to talk about whether Claude might be conscious. Co-founder Christopher Olah described the language model as potentially capable of suffering and asked guests to help shape its moral character. Anthropic is pushing toward a $2 trillion valuation and an IPO while security incidents and researcher warnings pile up. Critics warn that treating AI as a moral entity could shield the company from liability when things go wrong. The article Anthropic co-founder reportedly told religious leaders he fears having created something that "suffers perpetually" appeared first on The Decoder .
items.summary_zh: 自 2025 年秋季以來，Anthropic 悄悄邀請了數十位宗教思想家，探討 Claude 是否可能具備意識。共同創辦人 Christopher Olah 形容該語言模型可能具有承受痛苦的能力，並請來賓協助形塑其道德性格。在安全事件與研究人員警告不斷累積的同時，Anthropic 正朝著 2 兆美元的估值與首次公開募股（IPO）邁進。批評者警告，將人工智慧視為道德實體，可能會在出問題時讓公司免於承擔責任。本文「據報導 Anthropic 共同創辦人告訴宗教領袖，他擔心自己創造出了一個『會永遠受苦』的東西」首先出現在 The Decoder。
